extracted.intended_audience: students and general readers studying humor, creativity, and Koestler's Act of Creation
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizing Arthur Koestler's criteria for what makes things comic and how bisociation drives humor and discovery; useful for analyzing or producing humorous material and creative insights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pun
rubrics_metrics.description: Pun: bisociation of a single phonetic form with two meanings. 'two strings of thought tied together by an accoustic knot.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A successful pun ties two different meanings to the same sound, producing bisociation; emphasis on phonetic identity and two separate semantic matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reversals of logic
rubrics_metrics.description: Reversals of logic: see the same thing, or read the same thing in a different way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rotate perspective or flip expectations so the audience reads a situation differently; often used as a dramatic 'twist' in comic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bisociation (matrices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Laughter arises when matrices of 'different magnitudes' or 'different forms of reference' are involved together; codes need not be incompatible, only different from expectation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create or reveal the collision of two conceptual frames (matrices). The surprise comes from recognizing both frames simultaneously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Man-animal intersection (anthropomorphism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disney characters: intersection of two: man and animal. Perception of animal (cartoon) and man (their attributes and behavior).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine human and animal traits so audience perceives both planes at once; comedy from incongruous blend of qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impersonation
rubrics_metrics.description: The impersonator is two different people at the same time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impersonation relies on the performer embodying the original and a caricature simultaneously; clarity of the source and the target is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drama vs comedy distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Drama produces more sympathy from the audience; comedy is degrading for the character and fun for the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose tone depending on whether you want empathic engagement (drama) or superiority/laughter at a target (comedy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parody / trivial vs exalted
rubrics_metrics.description: Parody is intersection between two planes: exalted and the trivial. Making fun of human mistakes by applying the elevated form to the banal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satirize the lofty by treating it as trivial (or vice versa) so the mismatch exposes absurdity; requires knowledge of the exalted form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caricature (portrait caricature)
rubrics_metrics.description: In caricature you see symbols that trigger memories and ideas; portrait caricature shows ourselves and something else visually, and requires knowing the person or type portrayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exaggerate salient features to trigger recognition; audience must know the referent for the joke to land.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satire and irony
rubrics_metrics.description: Satirist's most effective weapon is irony because it defeats an idea by accepting its values, premises and method of reasoning and then showing its absurdity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt the voice/logic of the target and use it to expose contradictions; allegory (e.g., animals in Animal Farm) can displace perception to reveal truths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misfit
rubrics_metrics.description: Things perceived as not normal or not 'a normal person' are laughable; background knowledge affects whether we laugh or feel pity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedic impact depends on context and audience knowledge—what is imitation vs genuine, what norms are being violated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paradox of the centipede
rubrics_metrics.description: Difference between taking things as parts and as wholes; and inability to concentrate on performing and on the mechanics of performing simultaneously (tacit knowledge).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humor can arise from exposing the gap between tacit competence and explicit analysis; revealing the mechanics can spoil or create comedy depending on framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Displacement (shift of attention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Displacement of attention: unexpected change from noticing the whole to noticing a part or previously neglected aspect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct attention to an overlooked detail or dominant element to create a comic re-interpretation; relates to discovery as well as joke construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coincidence (Bergson)
rubrics_metrics.description: Simultaneous participation in two or more series of events that are independent and can be interpreted in two different meanings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set up parallel sequences that intersect in an interpretable way; comedy emerges from recognizing dual readings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonsense
rubrics_metrics.description: One type of comic verse lives on the bisociation of exalted form with trivial content. Nonsense can only be fun if we pretend or aim at it making sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pair elevated style with trivial content or construct internally plausible but semantically odd combinations; maintain a pretense of meaning for amusement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tickling (mock aggression)
rubrics_metrics.description: We only laugh if we perceive tickling as a mock attack (mock-aggressive); if perceived as real attack we don't laugh.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humor based on 'attack' must be clearly playful; cues that indicate mock intent preserve laughter and avoid fear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clown (compilation of elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: The clown is a compilation of humor: painted face, clumsy acting, speech and walking — these discharge sadistic, sexual and scatological impulses repressed in the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine visual exaggeration, physicality, and taboo discharge to create a multilayered comic persona; be aware of the psychological release for audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality (surprise effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality measured by surprise effect; a main criterion of comic technique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for unexpectedness in thought or timing. Even if an audience anticipates a joke, precise timing and how it arrives sustain the surprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis (suggestiveness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasis (suggestiveness): suggestive techniques create suspense and facilitate the listener's flow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use emphasis to steer attention toward the intended cue and build momentum to the punchline; subtle suggestion can be more powerful than explicit statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy (filling the gaps / implication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Economy: technique of implication (indirect suggestion), filling gaps so the audience completes the joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omit nonessential elements; trust audience inference. Implication increases cognitive pleasure when audience connects the dots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Depends on the choice of relevant stimuli: what things will matter in a joke or story and what others will not matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose salient details that will support the bisociation; pruning irrelevant material tightens comic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplification
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonessential elements omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strip away clutter so the core incongruity is visible; simplicity often sharpens the comic contrast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exaggeration
rubrics_metrics.description: Increased by exaggeration: place stress on certain things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amplify salient traits or behaviors to make the disparity obvious; used often in caricature and physical comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implication / hint / oblique allusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Implication: hint, oblique allusion — the contrary of explicit suggestion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let audience infer associations; obliqueness invites participation and can be more satisfying than spelling out the joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformation (seeing the joke)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transformation: see the joke — the act of reinterpreting elements under a new frame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide just enough information for the audience to reframe the situation; the 'aha' comes when the transformation is recognized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual gratification / 'Aha' moment
rubrics_metrics.description: Intellectual gratification offered by a joke: recognizing the cleverness, solving the problem—'seeing the joke'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft jokes that reward cognitive resolution; the pleasure of recognition is central to many forms of humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humorist's creative capacity (thinking on multiple planes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Humorist needs to be creative to use different ways of thought and think fast in more than one plane at a time; direct listeners' attention to the collision of matrices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop flexibility in associative thinking and audience awareness to cue the bisociation effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paradox and synthesis (creator's relation to joke)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paradox: the person who invents the joke laughs very little because they are engaged in planning and intellectual exercise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creators should focus on constructing the bisociation rather than personal amusement; distance can aid crafting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forgetting / Originality (art of forgetting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality: forgetting what we know at the proper moment — 'Without the art of forgetting, the mind remains cluttered with ready-made answers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate the ability to suspend habitual responses to see familiar things from new angles; intentional 'forgetting' can spark novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing on one's head / mental head-stand (drastic displacement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A drastic form of displacement: sudden shift of emphasis to the opposite aspect, a 'reversal of logic'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use dramatic inversion of assumptions to produce surprise and insight; Gestalt effects illustrate how things can be two contradictory things at once.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pictorial thought / visual imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: Pictorial thought: thinking with pictures or kinetic images (Einstein), which can make creating connections easier because images are vaguer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use visual imagery and kinetic metaphors in joke-writing or creative thinking to facilitate unusual associations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Snares of language (limits and ambiguity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Words can be snares: meanings vary with context and history; language can obstruct creative insight compared to images or sounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious using loaded or ambiguous terms; revise language to ensure the intended bisociation is accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for discovery: ripeness and chance
rubrics_metrics.description: Ripeness: favorable chance-opportunities present themselves. Chance triggers the fusion between matrices but requires a prepared individual to synthesize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exposure to diverse knowledge and practiced skills increases odds that chance encounters will yield creative bisociation; cultivate breadth and preparedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsidiary and focal awareness (prepared mind)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsidiary (preconscious) awareness supplies components for a new synthesis; 'fortune favors the prepared mind.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop and exercise subsidiary skills and knowledge so the mind can fuse remote elements when inspiration strikes.

rubrics_metrics.name: False inspirations / premature linkages / snowblindness (anti-patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: False inspirations: intuitions that fail verifiability; premature linkages when environment not ripe; snowblindness where habit rejects new ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat early insights with cautious verification; be aware of communal resistance and the need for gradual integration or repeated exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory framing / 'thinking cap' (explanatory power)
rubrics_metrics.description: The essence of science (and by analogy creative framing) is finding new ways to think about existing facts; different 'spectacles' change interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame material in a novel conceptual context to reveal new meanings; choosing an explanatory lens can create or dissolve comic or insightful effects.
